name: Jochebed
title: Moses' Faithful Mother
summary: Jochebed was a Levite woman and the mother of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam. She is known for her courageous faith when she hid her newborn son Moses for three months to save him from Pharaoh's death decree against Hebrew baby boys, and then placed him in a basket among the reeds on the Nile. Her actions were crucial for Israel's future deliverance from Egypt.

keyEvents.title: Jochebed's Family Relations
keyEvents.description: Jochebed was a daughter of Levi, born in Egypt. She married Amram, who also belonged to the tribe of Levi.

keyEvents.title: Moses' Birth and Hiding
keyEvents.description: When Moses was born, Jochebed saw that he was a beautiful child. In faith, she hid him for three months to protect him from Pharaoh's command to kill all Hebrew baby boys.

keyEvents.title: The Basket on the Nile
keyEvents.description: When Jochebed could no longer hide Moses, she made a basket of papyrus, sealed it with tar and pitch, put the child in it, and placed it among the reeds by the bank of the Nile.

keyEvents.title: Pharaoh's Daughter Finds Moses
keyEvents.description: Pharaoh's daughter found the child by the river. Miriam, Moses' sister, offered to get a Hebrew nurse, and brought Jochebed so that she could nurse her own child.

keyEvents.title: Jochebed Nurses and Raises Moses
keyEvents.description: Jochebed was paid by Pharaoh's daughter to nurse her own child. She raised Moses in his early years before he was brought to Pharaoh's court.

keyEvents.title: Testimony of Faith
keyEvents.description: The book of Hebrews highlights the faith of Moses' parents, who in faith hid their child for three months without fearing the king's command, showing Jochebed's deep trust in God.
